items.title: UN Talks Fail to Agree on Binding Rules for Autonomous Weapons
items.summary: Delegates at the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva ended a week of negotiations on November 21 with only a commitment to 'elaborate' on possible rules for lethal autonomous weapons over the next two years, leaving room for nonbinding measures. The International Committee of the Red Cross, the UN Secretary-General and Pope Leo XIV had urged a legally binding treaty within a year. NPR reported that Russia delayed proceedings by objecting to the agenda on day one, while the United States proposed a five-year window for optional guidelines. Nearly 100 countries had pushed for swift binding rules, but the convention's 128 members require consensus. Stop Killer Robots called the mandate watered down, noting that AI-enabled systems already select targets in active conflicts.
items.impact: The stalemate leaves a governance vacuum while AI-guided drones and targeting systems are already used in Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan. For vendors and governments, export controls and procurement rules rather than a treaty will shape deployment for years. Civilian-protection advocates say the delay raises humanitarian risk as capability outpaces diplomacy.

items.title: Google Puts AI Chat History on Its Homepage Sidebar
items.summary: Google is rolling out a redesigned desktop homepage globally that gives AI Mode a permanent foothold on the internet's most visited page. A collapsible panel opens from a gray bar on the left, listing recent AI Mode searches with options to start a new thread, search old ones or connect a Gemini Notebook. Under the search box, new shortcuts for creating images, asking about files and brainstorming have replaced the familiar Google Search button for signed-in users; pressing Enter still performs a normal search, and the button remains for signed-out visitors. Google's vice president of product Robby Stein said the sidebar addresses questions that are 'not just one and done' and helped users keep exploring in tests. The change follows an AI Mode button added last year and longer, AI-autocompleted queries in May.
items.impact: Placing saved AI conversations one click from the search box reframes searching as an ongoing session rather than a single query, intensifying competition with ChatGPT and Perplexity. Publishers should watch referral traffic as more tasks finish inside AI Mode, while privacy-conscious users should review Gemini Apps Activity, since uploads and prompts may feed model training unless opt-out settings are enabled.

items.title: FBI and USDA Reportedly Breached in Separate Cyberattacks
items.summary: The FBI is investigating an intrusion into the National Crime Information Center, the shared database that federal, state and local law enforcement use for warrants, criminal records and missing-person alerts, CNN reported. It is the bureau's second reported hack in months after a September incident allegedly exposing records of all FBI employees and applicants. Separately, NBC reported that the Department of Agriculture was breached this week; the known scope is its payments database, but former officials warned Reuters the compromised system could offer a path to food-safety data and animal-borne-illness research. President Trump confirmed the FBI hack in a Fox News interview. The disclosures follow a week of major FAA and NSA outages and the resignation of the White House national cyber director.
items.impact: Two core government systems hit within days points to sustained pressure on aging federal infrastructure and raises operational as well as data risk: NCIC integrity affects policing nationwide. With the national cyber director's post vacant, the incidents will intensify congressional scrutiny of cyber funding, MFA enforcement and how agencies segment payment and research networks from sensitive databases.

items.title: OpenRouter Warns MiniMax Prompts May Have Been Read After Canary Study
items.summary: Dragos chief research officer HD Moore seeded nearly two million AI prompts with unique, trackable secrets and found what he described as a privacy disaster across the inference supply chain. Ars Technica reports attackers had compromised at least three hosting providers, using stolen AWS keys in tens of thousands of API calls to probe S3 buckets, secrets managers and cloud identities. Some inference marketplaces simply logged customer prompts. A Chinese AI lab fetched secret URLs from more than half of prompts sent to its models between July and October, including roughly two-thirds marked 'no data collection' or Zero Data Retention; some scrapers returned days later, and a git client tried to clone private repositories named in prompts. On November 21, OpenRouter emailed customers that prompts routed to MiniMax models may have been read, removed Zero Data Retention labels from the affected endpoints, and named AtlasCloud, Novita and StreamLake as forwarders.
items.impact: The study shows a retention promise only binds the first hop: routers and resellers decrypt prompts at each stage, and a 'US provider' label may still route data offshore. Enterprises should stop placing credentials and signed URLs in prompts, pin upstream providers and rotate any secrets sent through affected routes. Regulators may treat zero-retention claims as misleading.

items.title: Dutch Regulator Finds AI Glasses Recording Lights Easy to Defeat
items.summary: The Dutch Data Protection Authority tested six AI camera glasses sold in the Netherlands, priced from under 100 euros to more than 500 euros, and advised consumers against buying them for general use. On nearly all devices the recording indicator was hard to see or easy to cover, and most kept filming after the light was obscured. Several models had weaknesses that let nearby people connect without authorization, access recordings or control the camera. Users were not always told where images and audio were processed, with data frequently sent to servers outside the EU. In simulated safety tests, one device falsely claimed an ambulance had been called during a resuscitation emergency and erred on medicine, weather and toy-safety questions. The authority did not name manufacturers; a separate lawsuit by Consumentenbond against Meta is due to be heard on November 26.
items.impact: The findings give regulators concrete evidence that bystander safeguards marketed for smart glasses fail in real products, directly testing the EDPB's rule that recording must stop when indicators are covered. Expect tighter product rules and retailer pressure in Europe, and treat AI-generated safety advice from wearables as unreliable until vendors demonstrate audit-tested controls.
